title: Exploring the effectiveness of ChatGPT-based feedback compared with teacher feedback and self-feedback: Evidence from Chinese to English translation
extended_summary:
This study asks whether ChatGPT-based feedback can improve translation performance as effectively as teacher feedback and self-feedback. The authors focus on a gap in the literature around the real effectiveness of ChatGPT as a feedback tool for language learning, especially when compared directly with human-provided feedback and self-revision.

The intervention is a three-condition comparison of revised Chinese-to-English translations: ChatGPT-based feedback, teacher feedback, and self-feedback. Participants were 45 advanced Master of Translation and Interpreting students at a top Chinese university. Each student translated the same Chinese press release into English and then revised their draft under each feedback condition, with two-week intervals between conditions to reduce carry-over effects. The authors evaluated outputs using BLEU for overall translation quality and Coh-Metrix/CFA/SEM analyses for lexical, syntactic, and cohesion-related features.

The main finding was that teacher feedback and self-feedback outperformed ChatGPT-based feedback on overall translation quality, while ChatGPT showed strengths in lexical enhancement and referential cohesion. Teacher feedback was better for syntax, especially verb phrase use and passive voice, and none of the three conditions significantly improved deep cohesion. The paper concludes that ChatGPT has promise as a supplementary tool, but it is not yet a replacement for teacher-led feedback in translation practice, particularly for advanced learners and syntax-sensitive tasks.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's conversational large language model chatbot used to generate feedback and responses from user prompts.
identified_tools.use_case: Used to generate feedback on students' Chinese-to-English translation drafts and compare its feedback effects against teacher feedback and self-feedback.

findings.finding_summary: In a sample of 45 advanced Chinese MTI students (135 revised translation texts across three feedback types), ChatGPT-based feedback produced the lowest overall translation quality by BLEU score (M=0.472) compared with teacher feedback (M=0.501) and self-feedback (M=0.485). The paper notes that an increase of 0.02 in BLEU is widely considered meaningful, so ChatGPT-based feedback lagged behind the other two conditions on this overall measure.
findings.measure: BLEU score for overall translation quality

findings.finding_summary: ChatGPT-based feedback yielded the highest lexical scores among the three conditions, outperforming both self-feedback and teacher feedback on the lexicon latent factor. At the indicator level, it produced longer average word length and more specific verbs, with significant main effects reported for DESWLlt (F(2,132)=16.181, p<.001, ηp2=.197) and WRDHYPv (F(2,132)=12.269, p<.001, ηp2=.157).
findings.measure: Lexicon latent factor; word length (DESWLlt); verb specificity/hypernymy (WRDHYPv)

findings.finding_summary: For syntax, ChatGPT-based feedback was less effective than teacher feedback and self-feedback. The paper reports that teacher feedback scored higher than ChatGPT-based feedback on the syntax latent factor, and on specific indicators teacher feedback led to denser verb phrases and more agentless passive voice than ChatGPT-based feedback (e.g., DRVP: F(2,132)=3.405, p<.05, ηp2=.049; DRPVAL: F(2,132)=9.686, p<.001, ηp2=.128).
findings.measure: Syntax latent factor; verb phrase density (DRVP); agentless passive voice (DRPVAL)

findings.finding_summary: ChatGPT-based feedback did not significantly improve cohesion overall relative to teacher feedback or self-feedback. The authors report no significant main effect for cohesion across the three feedback types (F(2,132)=2.368, p>.05), and no significant effect on deep cohesion (PCDCz: F(2,132)=.618, p=.54), although referential cohesion was higher under ChatGPT than the other conditions (PCREFp: F(2,132)=4.401, p<.05, ηp2=.063).
findings.measure: Cohesion latent factor; referential cohesion (PCREFp); deep cohesion (PCDCz)

quality_tier_rationale: This is a single empirical comparative study with a modest sample and no randomized classroom intervention design described in the excerpt. It provides quantitative evidence, but the design and reporting do not rise to the level of high-causality experimental evidence.
impact_tier_rationale: The study shows a meaningful negative effect on overall translation quality for ChatGPT-based feedback and a positive effect on lexicon, with reported effect sizes that are modest to medium (e.g., ηp2=.157-.197). Overall impact is mixed rather than uniformly large.
